review.summary: WP05 final acceptance cannot be granted yet. In the supplied storage and response code I found no code-level blocker. Several protections are in place: only an opaque status goes in the URL, and an HttpOnly cookie carries the draft key. The draft is encrypted with AES-GCM and bound to its lookup hash, form, source path and expiry. Writes need an exact Origin match and a valid source path, and fail closed when storage fails. An advisory lock in a ReadCommitted transaction enforces the row cap, and field keys are checked against the form's allowlist. Building the answers object with defineProperty blocks prototype pollution. The prior qualified reviews in the lineage cover the other files; I combined their results and did not reread those files. The blocking gap is evidence: the browser matrix for native lp/partner pages and statuses is still running (16 cases pass), but R6 cites 27 current browser cases. The task itself says the gate must wait. Already accepted and not repeated as findings: the manual Stop/Esc check pending until reload (nonblocking MINOR) and the ASCII-only path boundary for raw or encoded paths (documented MINOR). One new MINOR: a few clients can keep the shared 128-row draft cap full, which silently disables field preservation for every user. This does not approve deployment or confirm the overall goal is complete.

The lineage shows lp/[slug] and lp/[slug]/[stepPath] pages were changed by the attribution amendments, so their native browser behavior is not covered by older results.

findings.recommended_fix: Hold the WP05 acceptance gate until the remaining native lp/partner/status browser cases finish. Then change the R6 evidence to the actual current pass count, tied to snapshot c4bb7750….
findings.required_test: Finish the native browser matrix: statuses 400/403/404/429/503 on /lp/{slug}, /lp/{slug}/{step}, and the partner (/p) page. Each case must show a 303 back to the source page, only the opaque registrationRetry status in the URL, fields refilled, the shared aria-live/alert feedback, no serious or critical axe findings, and a 503 resubmit leaving count 1. Record the total pass count against the current snapshot hash.

findings.area: REGISTRATION_RETRY_MAX_ROWS=128 global cap; registrationRetryResponse rate limit 'registration-retry-draft' 10/60s
findings.issue: All users share one cap of 128 draft rows, each living 10 minutes. Each client can write 10 drafts per minute. A non-browser client can set the Origin header and post deliberately invalid data to a public active form, which triggers the 400 path, so about two clients can keep the cap full indefinitely. After that, every legitimate native error redirect gets registrationRetry=unavailable and loses its fields. clearRegistrationRetry also deletes any earlier draft the user had.
findings.evidence: trustedNativeRetryRequest only compares the Origin header, which works as CSRF protection, not authentication. eligibleDraftFields only needs a public active form. Statuses 400 and 429 both save drafts. The in-lock count() >= 128 returns null for all callers. The rate limit is per request (presumably per IP): 10/min × 10-min TTL ≈ 100 rows per client.
findings.impact: This only affects availability: the R1 field-preservation guarantee can be cheaply switched off for everyone. Behavior stays fail-closed, with no PII exposure or duplicate submissions, so this does not block the authorized scope.
findings.recommended_fix: Treat this as a documented residual risk, or propose a scope change: cap active drafts per rate-limit key, raise the global cap within the storage budget, or reserve part of the capacity. Keep the fail-closed behavior.
findings.required_test: DB test: one key fills its quota, and a draft from a different key still saves; or document and test the accepted saturation behavior.
